# Sirach Chapter 42 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic Equivalent)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 42 | **Date:** 2026-03-17

---

**42:1** Do not let false shame lead you into sin. There are things you should not be embarrassed about:

**42:2** the law of the Most High and his covenant, or rendering a verdict that exposes the guilty;

**42:3** settling financial accounts with a business partner or a traveling companion, or dividing an inheritance among heirs;

**42:4** accurate scales and honest weights, and whether you're acquiring a lot or a little;

**42:5** making a fair profit in commerce, and disciplining children firmly, or flogging a dishonest slave until he bleeds.

**42:6** If you have a treacherous wife, keep things under lock and seal; where you have many employees, keep everything locked up.

**42:7** Whatever you hand over to others, do it by count and measure; and put every transaction in writing.

**42:8** Don't be ashamed to correct the ignorant or the foolish, even an old man corrected by a young one. Then you will be truly educated, approved before all living people.

**42:9** A daughter is a secret source of anxiety to her father; worry about her keeps him awake: will she pass her prime unmarried? When she marries, will her husband hate her?

**42:10** While she is a virgin, will she be violated and get pregnant in her father's house? When she lives with a husband, will she be unfaithful? After she marries, will she be barren?

**42:11** Keep a firm grip on a headstrong daughter — otherwise she'll make you the laughingstock of your enemies, the talk of the town, an embarrassment in public, a scandal in the city gate.

**42:12** Don't stare at any man's handsome face; don't sit around among women;

**42:13** for moths come from clothing, and a woman's trouble comes from women.

**42:14** Better even a man's wickedness than a woman who does good and shames you with it.

**42:15** Now I will call to mind the works of the Lord; what I have seen I will put into words. By the Lord's command his works came into existence.

**42:16** The blazing sun surveys everything, and the work of the Lord is saturated with his glory.

**42:17** Not even to his holy ones has the Lord granted the power to tell all his wonders — those that the Lord Almighty has established, so that the whole universe stands firm through his glory.

**42:18** He plumbs the depths and the human heart; he sees through every clever scheme. For the Most High knows everything there is to know; he reads the signs of the age,

**42:19** announcing what has already happened and what is yet to come, uncovering traces of what was hidden.

**42:20** Not a thought escapes him; not a single word is concealed from him.

**42:21** He has arranged the grand works of his wisdom in order; he is from everlasting to everlasting. Nothing can be added to him or removed, and he needs no one to advise him.

**42:22** How magnificent are all his works — worth marveling at, down to the tiniest spark!

**42:23** All these things go on forever, enduring through every age; they are all obedient to him in every need.

**42:24** Everything exists in pairs — opposites balancing each other — and he has left nothing incomplete.

**42:25** Each thing enhances the good of the other. Who could ever see enough of his glory?
